page: Amazon Web Services r5n.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading support. System memory capacity is 256.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration integrates a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface. It does not include bundled local instance storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes for disk operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate multi-threaded capacity alongside lower single-threaded execution metrics. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 9818.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 25487.55, while single-core processing registered 1109.0 in Geekbench and 1286.4 in stress-ng. Data compression tests reflect this trend, with single-threaded gzip compression at 21.8 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 8.25 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 103.3 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth reached 47.59 GB/sec. The instance handled 25.79 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 20.75 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Resource allocation on this instance prioritizes memory density and network throughput over aggressive per-core compute performance. Because local NVMe storage is absent, input and output performance depends directly on the 25 Gbps network interface connected to block storage. The system profile fits memory-intensive applications such as in-memory caches, distributed key-value stores, relational databases requiring substantial buffer space, and large-scale data manipulation jobs.
